A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ECTraj research despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original Argoverse 2 predictions, qualitative comparisons and ablations, including appendix experiments on scheduling, fusion, sampling steps and priors.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds Waymo results, measured inference times and a U-turn failure example.

M1.justification: The QCNet-conditioned consistency model, latent mapping, best-of-six training, midpoint/endpoint teacher fusion and single-step inference remain unchanged. Scheduling expressions are corrected against the already-described curriculum; the PDFs do not establish a distinct new method.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates only Argoverse 2. V2 adds actual evaluation on the Waymo Open Motion Dataset in Appendix Section 3, extending coverage to another driving dataset with 11 historical and 80 future frames, versus Argoverse 2's 50 and 60.

E2.justification: The Argoverse 2 accuracy comparator set is unchanged. V2 adds standalone QCNet comparisons in the timing measurements, U-turn example and Waymo evaluation, including reported official QCNet results and the authors' own run. QCNet is distinct from the retained QCNeXt comparator.

E3.justification: V2 introduces per-scenario wall-clock measurements separating denoising, QCNet and their combined cost. Its new Waymo evaluation uses QCNet trained from scratch because a checkpoint was unavailable. Existing Argoverse training settings are retained; the added joint-metric terminology and sampling explanation do not establish changed evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 and Figure 3 add a U-turn failure case comparing ECTraj, OptTrajDiff and QCNet. V2 also analyzes denoising overhead relative to QCNet across datasets. The existing component, scheduling, fusion, sampling-step and prior ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, variability estimates or significance tests for experimental results. V2 adds average inference times without uncertainty estimates or a disclosed repetition protocol.

E6.justification: Existing Argoverse benchmark and ablation values are unchanged. New Waymo results report ADE6/FDE6 of 0.83/1.75 for ECTraj, 0.95/2.02 for OptTrajDiff and 0.77/1.62 for the authors' QCNet run. New combined QCNet-plus-denoising times are 27.81 versus 54.55 ms on Argoverse 2 and 44.49 versus 77.50 ms on Waymo for ECTraj versus OptTrajDiff.

T1.justification: Appendix Section 1.1 changes the teacher-schedule exponent from floor to ceiling and adds the missing constant 1 to n(t'), matching the main formulation. Algorithm 1 changes N from 10*2^ceil(e/(3E)) to 10*2^floor(3e/E). These are limited mathematical corrections; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: enhanced teacher supervision, best-of-K consistency training, competitive Argoverse 2 accuracy and one-tenth of OptTrajDiff's inference steps. The revised title and clearer train-from-scratch description do not change those claims.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly acknowledges missing joint-prediction confidence scores and U-turn failures, and hypothesizes that teacher fusion helps in the illustrated failure case. The Waymo discussion explains the failure to reproduce official QCNet performance and reinforces the existing prior-dependence limitation. It also offers a compression-based explanation for differing relative computational overhead.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository pointer and specifies six independent inference samples without post-processing, contrasting this with OptTrajDiff's 128 predictions and clustering. It documents training QCNet for Waymo and retaining ten-dimensional latents. Existing hardware and main training hyperparameters remain unchanged; repository availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds the Waymo dataset citation and qualifies OptTrajDiff as the joint diffusion-based Argoverse comparator. The related-work discussion otherwise retains its positioning. Additional bibliography entries for OptTrajDiff and QCNet duplicate already-cited works rather than introducing new research.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper, updates affiliations and running headers, makes local language and explanation edits, and merges the limitations subsection into the conclusion. Short discussions and a Waymo appendix section are added, while the overall narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 adds the U-turn figure, an Argoverse timing table and two Waymo tables. The main benchmark table gains year and venue columns. Existing figures and tables are retained with local resizing, relocation, caption formatting and pagination changes.

improvement.justification: V2 improves empirical transparency through QCNet-inclusive timing, additional dataset evidence and explicit failure reporting. The timing tables reveal roughly twofold total acceleration on Argoverse 2, alongside tenfold denoising acceleration. Formula corrections and additional implementation disclosures also help. Gains remain limited: broad speedup wording persists, the official Waymo QCNet performance was not reproduced, and uncertainty reporting remains absent.
